pairs.difference: A: the pumpkins are one pushed orange from lit side to shadow side, and the fence repeats that orange against loud green grass. Hero and background are equally loud (0.148 vs 0.143), and shadows under the leaves go to dark olive. B: the topiary is green on green, with a pale neutral plinth and path to rest the eye, and its warm share is very low. B is restrained; A is the more hue-pushed. It is a weak lean, because both sit inside the real ranges.
pairs.fix: Make the pumpkins a dusty, slightly brownish orange with muted, cooler plum-brown shadows on their undersides. Keep the fence a greyed natural wood and soften the grass green so the pumpkins stand out.

pairs.difference: A: the red cooler has a violet shadow on the sand, matching the real cards' cool shadows, and its inner lid is a cream-white neutral. B: the marble lion is very low chroma (0.027, below the real range), but a pale stone statue can honestly be that neutral. It has warm cream lights and grey-taupe shadows on a saturated green scene. Both cards carry cream neutrals, so that lesson does not separate them. The low subject chroma comes from the material, not from a colour fault.

A: the bat collapses to a single flat purple mass in the lens, set on a yellow-orange spiral. It is a pure complementary pairing with warm share 0.82, above the real range, and shadow chroma at 0.72, just below it. There is almost no neutral and no secondary hue. B: the cream envelope gives a large resting neutral between saturated green and the small multi-hue photos. Its shadow chroma is high, but the colour roles are clearly layered.
pairs.fix: Paint the bat in a greyed, dusty plum with cooler blue-grey shadows and warmer brownish fur tips. Make the wing membranes a muted mauve, and calm the background to a softer yellow.

pairs.difference: B: the cauldron is nearly colourless charcoal (subject 0.057, below the real range), and its shadows lose chroma (0.525) on a hot pure magenta wall with a lime brew. The hero has little local colour between the neon accents, and hue families are at the real floor. The mauve-grey ledge is the only rest. A: the shoes are busy (5.49 hue families, above range), with blue, green, teal and pink on an orange and pale yellow setting. The hero stays chromatic and its shadows keep their colour. A has a real flaw in its rainbow count, but B has more fields out of range.
pairs.fix: Give the cauldron a colourful deep blue-violet iron with rich indigo shadows rather than neutral black. Soften the wall from hot magenta to a dustier pink-purple and make the brew a slightly less neon green.

pairs.difference: B: the candelabra reads as a single pushed golden-orange mass in the lens, with cream wax and a clean pure cyan background. That is the warm-cream and pure-hue habit the lessons show on generated cards. A: the lamp is a muted dark teal related to its background, with soft yellow-green glass, so the colour is restrained and believable. A's numbers run low (subject 0.064, shadow 0.54), which makes this a modest lean on the eye.
pairs.fix: Make the brass an aged, slightly greenish-brown metal with darker cool shadows instead of even bright gold. Keep the wax a cooler off-white and slightly dull the cyan background.

pairs.difference: B: the house wall, trim and roof merge into red-brown and maroon masses in the lens. Pure yellow glowing windows and a sky at 0.151, slightly above the real background range, are added on top. Hue families are high at 5.82, and the wall shadows turn plum-red nearly everywhere. A: the door keeps a believable blue local colour with blue shadows, the frame stays wood orange, and the flowers are small accents. Its chroma sits inside the real range, and the hue roles are clear.
pairs.fix: Keep the walls a cool grey-lavender stone with blue-violet shadows rather than red-brown. Tone the windows down to a soft pale yellow, reduce the purple on the roof, and make the sky a calmer blue.

pairs.difference: A: the gravestone's subject chroma is very low (0.047, below range) and warm share is 0.038, also below range, while shadow chroma is above range at 1.49. In the lens, the moss, grass and stone shadows all fall into one yellow-olive family, so shadows pick up green rather than a related cool. B: the slide is a loud green on pink with a blue ladder, but every field sits inside the real ranges and the white tile deck rests the eye. The stone's neutrality is legitimate, so this lean is modest.
pairs.fix: Tint the stone a light cool blue-grey with faint warm patches and soft violet shadows. Make the moss a slightly deeper natural green so it differs from the grass.

pairs.difference: A: the coral-orange fills wall and ledge in one mass, and it also bleeds into the silver stand, which turns pink-peach in the lens. The whole lower card is pulled warm around a blue-violet orb. B: the vending machine is blue on purple, with small multi-hue cans and clean pale blue glass. Its neutrals stay cool, and the shadow chroma is kept. B is near-monochrome cold (warm share 0.026, below range), but its local colours hold up. This is a slight lean.
pairs.fix: Keep the stand a clean cool silver with blue-grey shadows, without an orange tint. Make the wall a softer peach and separate the ledge with a slightly different muted tone.

pairs.difference: B: the handle, bristles and floor all land in one orange mass in the lens, with the same orange-brown for shadows. The hero and floor are not separated by hue, and hue families are low at 2.6 on a warm-leaning card with teal behind it. A: the red mower, cool grey handle and dark wheels, green grass and cyan background each hold their own hue. It has real neutrals in the metal and tyres, even though the shadows go greyish (0.41, below range).
pairs.fix: Make the bristles a pale dry straw and the handle a darker reddish brown. Make the floor a muted grey-brown wood, and give the shadow on the floor a cool purple-brown.

pairs.difference: A: the coffin and floor share one orange-wood family, with the shadows also a deep orange-brown. The card is warm-biased at 0.65, with hue families at 2.78, below the real range, and only a green wall as relief. Both lit and shadow sides stay orange, and the only rest is a little brass. B: the chair also has wood on wood, but the blue wall and lime cushion give clear hue roles, the floor shadow reads cool, and the wood runs from pale yellow to deep brown-orange.
pairs.fix: Make the coffin a darker, cooler red-brown wood with plum-brown shadows. Make the floor a pale greyed tan so it differs from the coffin, and give the shadow on the floor a cool violet-brown.

pairs.difference: A: the violet burst reaches 0.25 chroma, above the real background range, and the pumpkin is a loud pure orange and yellow with little neutral on the card. Hero and background shout equally, and the pumpkin's shadow side stays orange-red. B: the jacket keeps believable muted khaki with orange trim and a deep green sash on a calmer green, so the neutral tan rests the eye.
pairs.fix: Lower the background to a dusty muted violet. Make the pumpkin a natural, slightly brownish orange with deep cool red-brown shadows, and keep the bright yellow only inside the carved face.

pairs.difference: A: the towel is orange and yellow on green, with background chroma at 0.217, right at the top of the real range, but its colour logic is simple and consistent. Folds shift to deeper orange. B: the coral is pink and orange on soft green, close to the real coral card, with plum rocks. Its shadow chroma is low at 0.546, though the rocks are cool and related. Each has one small numeric flag, pointing in different directions, and neither shows a clear hue fault.

pattern: The lessons run consistently one way. Generated cards push local colour towards pure hue, with a more saturated orange leather, a brighter blue, and a more pure red. Neutrals drift to warm cream, where real cards keep cooler whites and greys with lavender or blue-grey shadows. Shadows on generated cards stay in the object's own orange or red family, or go olive, so the lens shows one flat hero mass, and wood or floor props fall into the same hue as the hero. Hero and background are equally loud, with little neutral to rest the eye. Overall this colour evidence is modest: most test calls are at confidence 2 to 3, and only p10 and p11 are strong. p02 and p12 give no colour reason to choose. Spooky subjects overlapped my picks and may have nudged the close calls, although subject matter is not a colour finding.
